decisive_items: Singular and large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells
Nuclear division and apoptotic cells present
Infiltration of blood vessels and adipose tissue
response.rationale: The lymph node biopsy shows large atypical proliferative lymphoid cells with mitoses, apoptosis, and invasive growth, diagnostic of lymphoma; multisystem nodal/extranodal PET findings and prolonged fever support advanced disease. Other candidates lack this histologic pattern and are contradicted by it.

rejected.why: Sarcoidosis would show non-caseating granulomas, not large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells with invasive growth.
Hyperuricemia-associated disease is only a past history and cannot explain lymphadenopathy or biopsy findings.
Infectious disease is nonspecific and contradicted by biopsy showing atypical lymphoid proliferation rather than organisms or granulomas.
Metastatic cancer can cause widespread lesions but biopsy indicates a lymphoid, not epithelial or solid malignancy.
Hyperuricemia is incidental and unrelated to nodal/extranodal disease.
Infection explains fever and respiratory symptoms but not the invasive large atypical lymphoid cells.
Tuberculosis may cause fever and mediastinal/lung cavities, but biopsy lacks granulomas and instead shows atypical lymphocytic infiltration.
Castleman disease can cause lymphadenopathy but not the large heterotypic, mitotically active, and invasive lymphoid cells seen here.
